answer: Each seat holds one accessioned object, its number dated a year before enrolment. A registrar files the catalogue entry and condition notes; then each epoch the seed names an angle, and the custodian re-shoots the piece from its nadir beside a dated scale bar, and the image must hash to that entry. Seats sharing an accession number, invoice or donor fold to one vote at 45,000 POA forfeit. Cataloguing runs $400 an object, so a thousand clones need a thousand clean pieces. A lantern pulled from a flooded shaft is a relic once its number is written, and no copy can be accessioned twice.
